questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the source of gonadotropin-releasing hormone?
questions.solution:
I. Hypothalamic hormones are of two types :
1. Releasing hormones - Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH).
2. Inhibiting hormones - Somatostatin.

II. Hormones of Adenohypophysis
1. Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) - Growth hormone (GH), Prolactin (PRL), Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), Adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), Luteinizing hormone (LH) and Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
2. Pars intermedia - Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).

III. Neurohypophysis (Pars nervosa or Posterior pituitary) - Oxytocin and Vasopressin (or ADH).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of organs includes only the endocrine glands?
questions.solution:
Parathyroid and Adrenal are the endocrine glands. Adrenal glands are the pairs of endocrine glands situated immediately above the kidneys. Hence they are also known as suprarenal glands.

Parathyroid glands are the two pairs of endocrine glands situated behind the thyroid gland in higher vertebrates. They produce parathyroid hormone, which controls the amount of calcium in the blood. The thymus is a temporary endocrine gland as its secretion decreases with age, while the pancreas, testis, and ovary are an example of heterocrine glands.

To increase cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids.

Cortisol is also involved in maintaining the cardiovascular system as well as the kidney functions. Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppress the immune response. Cortisol stimulates RBC production.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: ADH is synthesised by ___________, released by _____________ and acts on __________.
options: Hypothalamus, neurohypophysis, DCT and collecting duct
questions.solution: Vasopressin, also known as arginine vasopressin (AVP), antidiuretic hormone (ADH), or argipressin, is a neurohypophysial hormone found in most mammals. Its two primary functions are to retain water in the body and to constrict blood vessels. Vasopressin regulates the body's retention of water by acting to increase water reabsorption in the collecting ducts of the kidney nephron. Vasopressin is a peptide hormone that increases water permeability of the kidney's collecting duct and distal convoluted tubule increases peripheral vascular resistance, which in turn increases arterial blood pressure. It plays a key role in homeostasis, by the regulation of water, glucose, and salts in the blood. It is derived from a preprohormone precursor that is synthesized in the hypothalamus and stored in vesicles at the posterior pituitary.

questions.solution: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine  (also known as, catecholamines). They are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations, hence called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heartbeat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration. questions.solution:
Hormones bind to specific hormone receptors (proteins) which are of two types mainly:
A. Membrane-bound receptors (present on the cell membrane of the target cells) - Those hormones (protein or peptide) which bound to the membrane-bound receptors usually do not enter the target cell but generate second messengers like cyclic AMP, IP3, Ca++, etc. which in turn regulate cellular metabolism.
B. Intracellular receptors (receptors present inside the target cells - mostly nuclear receptors) - Hormones (e.g. steroid hormones, iodothyronines, etc.) which bound to intracellular receptors, usually regulate gene expression or chromosome function by the interaction of the hormone-receptor complex with the genome. Various biochemical actions occur resulting in physiological and developmental effects.

questions.solution:

questions.solution:
1.  Somatostatin is secreted by delta cells at several locations in the digestive system, namely, the pyloric antrum, the duodenum and the pancreatic islets.
2.  Melatonin is mainly produced by the pineal gland.
3.  Aldosterone, the main mineralocorticoid hormone, is a steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland. It is essential for sodium conservation in the kidney, salivary glands, sweat glands and colon.
4. Erythropoietin, also known as hematopoietic or hemopoietin, is a glycoprotein cytokine secreted by the kidney in response to cellular hypoxia; it stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow.
5. hCG (Human chorionic gonadotropin) is a hormone produced by the placenta after implantation. The presence of hCG is detected in some pregnancy tests.

On the other hand, parathormone promotes the mobilization of calcium from bones into blood hence causes demineralization.

The other listed hormones also contribute to osteoporosis but their effects are insignificant or very less, e.g., low level of progesterone and aldosterone causes bone loss, whereas the raised level of prolactin has been linked with osteoporosis.

2. Formation of corpus luteum from the remnants of the Graafian follicles after ovulation.
3. Maintains the corpus luteum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Name a peptide hormone which acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation.
questions.solution: Insulin is a peptide hormone which acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation decreasing the blood glucose level.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Coronavirus is highly dangerous and life-threatening for elderly. This is due to a progressive decrease in secretion of
questions.solution: The thymus is degenerated in elderly resulting in a decreased production of thymosins. As a result, the immune responses of the elderly become weak.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not the function of parathormone (PTH)?
options: Decreases the reabsorption of calcium from the renal tubules
Increases the calcium absorption from GIT
Decreases the movement of calcium to bones.
questions.solution:
Functions of the parathyroid hormone (PTH) includes:

A. PTH increases the process of bone resorption or dissolution (demineralization) of bone.
B. PTH stimulates the reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules.
C. PTH increases the absorption of Ca2+ from digested food.
D. All of the above actions of PTH increase the blood Ca2+ levels, thus PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone. PTH and Thyrocalcitonin play a significant role in maintaining the calcium balance in the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement regarding the pituitary gland from the following.
options: The pars distalis region of the adenohypophysis secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
GnRH is produced by the pituitary gland which stimulates the release of gonadotropins from the hypothalamus.
Oxytocin and vasopressin are produced by the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
The hypothalamus is under the direct neural regulation of the posterior pituitary.
questions.solution: The pituitary gland is divided into adenohypophysis which secretes its own hormones and neurohypophysis which stores and releases hormones by the hypothalamus. Oxytocin and vasopressin are produced by the hypothalamus and stored and released by the posterior pituitary.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the statements given below. Identify which of them are true and which of them are false. Select the correct option after referring to the given table.

A. The pituitary gland is present in a bony cavity of the skull known as sella tursica.
B. The pancreas is only an endocrine gland.
C. The diurnal rhythm of the body is maintained by the pineal gland.
D. Glucocorticoids stimulate glycolysis, lipolysis and proteolysis.
options: A- True, B- False, C-True, D- False
A- False, B- True, C-False, D- True
A- True, B- False, C-True, D- True
A- False, B- True, C-True, D- False
questions.solution: Pituitary gland is present in a bony cavity of the sphenoid bone of the skull known as sellaturcica. Pancreas is a heterocrine gland as it has endocrine (Islets of Langerhans) as well as exocrine (acini) components. Pineal gland also called the vestigial third eye secretes melatonin. Glucocorticoids produced from adrenal cortex stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is an important function of cortisol?
options: Maintains cardio-vascular system as well as the kidney functions.
questions.solution: Glucocorticoids like cortisol are mainly involved in carbohydrate metabolism. Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis. These inhibit cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids. Cortisol also helps in maintaining the cardiovascular system and the kidney functions. GCs (particularly cortisol) produce anti-inflammatory reactions and also suppress the immune response. Cortisol increases RBC production.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is mismatched?
options: Growth hormone - Promotes the physical growth of body.
questions.solution:
Functions of Parathormone (PTH) :

A. PTH increases the process of bone resorption or dissolution (demineralization) of bone.

B. PTH stimulates the reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules.

C. PTH increases the absorption of Ca2+ from digested food.

D. All the above actions of PTH increase the blood Ca2+ levels, thus PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements are true regarding the hypothalamus?
options: It is situated at the base of rhombencephalon.
It has centres for breathing and respiration.
It has centres which control body temperature, urge for eating and drinking.
It is connected to the posterior pituitary with hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system.
questions.solution: The hypothalamus has centres which control body temperature and the urge for eating and drinking. It is a part of forebrain and diencephalon. It is connected to the anterior pituitary with hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal system. The centres for breathing and respiration are present in pons and medulla.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following hormones of the human body are not secreted by an endocrine gland?
questions.solution: The atrial natriuretic factor or ANF is a peptide hormone secreted by the heart. The other hormones GH, parathyroid hormone and thyroxine are secreted by endocrine glands. These are referred to ductless glands which secrete the hormones directly into the bloodstream. The heart is not such a gland.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Aldosterone is secreted from
options: Zona glomerulosa - outer layer of adrenal cortex
Zona fasciculata - middle layer of adrenal cortex
Zona reticularis - inner layer of adrenal cortex
questions.solution: The adrenal cortex can be divided into three layers, called zona reticularis (inner layer) releases androgenic steroids, zona fasciculata (middle layer) releases glucocorticoids, and zona glomerulosa (outer layer) releases aldosterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which set of organs is designated as heterocrine glands?
questions.solution: Heterocrine glands mean the gland having endocrine (ductless parts secreting hormones) and exocrine parts (portions with ducts) both.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hormones A and B secreted by Islet of Langerhans cause hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, respectively
questions.solution: The α-cells of the Islets of Langerhans are responsible for the secretion of glucagon. Glucagon is responsible for glycogenolysis. Hence, it causes hyperglycemia. The β-cells of the Islet of Langerhans are responsible for the secretion of insulin. Insulin is responsible for glycogenesis and hence caused hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mucus secreted by the goblet cells, combined with bicarbonates maintains the alkaline medium of the intestine. The source of bicarbonates is:
questions.solution: The intestinal mucosal epithelium has goblet cells which secrete mucus. The secretions of the brush border cells of the mucosa along with the secretions of the goblet cells constitute the intestinal juice or succus entericus. This juice contains a variety of enzymes like disaccharidases (e.g., maltase), dipeptidases, lipases, nucleosidases, etc. The mucus along with the bicarbonates from the pancreas protects the intestinal mucosa from acid as well as provide an alkaline medium (pH 7.8) for enzymatic activities.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A student is about to appear for an examination in the next half an hour. He is extremely anxious. His face is flushed and his heartbeat has increased. Which of the following could be a probable reason for this?
options: Secretion of sleep-regulating hormones by the pineal gland
Secretion of glucocorticoids by the adrenal cortex
Secretion of TSH by the thyroid gland
Secretion of emergency hormones by the adrenal medulla
questions.solution: The adrenal medulla is responsible for secretion of hormones 'adrenaline' and 'noradrenaline', collectively known as 'catecholamines'. These hormones are also called as 'hormones of fight or flight' or 'emergency hormones'. They are responsible for the increase in heartbeat, respiratory rate, etc., in times of emergency situations in response to stress.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is synthesized by pars nervosa of the pituitary gland?
questions.solution: Hormones of posterior pituitary are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported to neurohypophysis via hypothalamic neurons, e.g., oxytocin and vasopressin (or ADH).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Good vision depends on adequate intake of carotene-rich food.

Select the best option from the following statements:

(i) Vitamin A derivatives are formed from carotene.
(ii) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment.
(iii) Retinal is a derivative of vitamin A.
(iv) Retinal is a light-absorbing part of all the visual photopigments.
questions.solution: Carotene is the source of retinal which is involved in the formation of rhodopsin of rod cells. Retinal, a derivative of vitamin A, is the light-absorbing part of all visual photopigments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following radioactive isotope will be used in the detection of thyroid cancer?
questions.solution: Iodine is an element used by the thyroid gland for the synthesis of thyroid hormones. Thus, radioactive isotope Iodine-131 is used as radioactive material for the detection of thyroid cancer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements (A–D):

1. Catecholamines secreted from adrenal medulla stimulate breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood.
2. Cortisol is also involved in maintaining the cardio-vascular system as well as kidney functions.
3. Hormone released from zona fasciculate produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response.
4. Androgenic steroids secreted by adrenal cortex play a role in growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.

How many of the above statements are true?
questions.solution: The adrenal medulla of the adrenal gland secretes two hormone epinephrine and norepinephrine, collectively called catecholamines, which are called fight or flight hormones. During this situation, energy is required which is also a function of catecholamines as it stimulates the breakdown of glycogen to give glucose. During fight and flight situation cortisol hormone (stress hormone) concentration also increases which is secreted by adrenal cortex cells, zona fasciculata. They increase blood pressure, suppress the immune response by activating anti-stress and anti-inflammatory pathway and increase glucose concentration. Androgens are sex hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex that control secondary sexual characters.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are steps involved in the mechanism of action of hormones. Arrange them in proper sequence and select the correct option.

I. Formation of the hormone-receptor complex.
II. Biochemical changes in the target cell.
III. Binding of the hormone with the receptor.
IV. Physiological responses in the target cell.
questions.solution:
The steps involved in the mechanism of action of hormones are as follows:

1. Hormones bind to a specific receptors situated on the target cell.

2. Binding of the hormone to receptor leads to the formation of hormone-receptor complex.

3. The hormone-receptor complex induces certain biochemical changes in the target cell.

4. The ultimate effect is the generation of the physiological response in the target cell.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the statements given below and select the correct option.
options: Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) is responsible for increasing the blood pressure.
Gastrin stimulates the secretion of HCl and trypsinogen.
Erythropoietin is produced by Juxta-Glomerular cells of the kidney.
CCK acts only on the gall bladder.
questions.solution:
I. Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) is a hormone secreted by the atrial wall of the heart. It is responsible for decreasing blood pressure.

II. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of HCl and pepsinogen.

III. Erythropoietin is produced by juxta glomerular cells of the kidney. It stimulates erythropoiesis.

IV. Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on the pancreas and gallbladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice respectively.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following is correct about the nature of hormones?

1. Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals.
2. Hormone act as intercellular messengers
3. Hormones are reusable
4. A hormone is produced by exocrine glands
questions.solution: Hormones are secreted by the endocrine cells in one part of the body and carried by the blood to another part where they stimulate or inhibit the specific physiological process. The hormones have low molecular weight molecules and are specific in their action. These acts in very low concentration, are quick-acting and are non-antigenic. The hormones are mostly short-lived and have no cumulative effect, after their action, they are removed from the liver and kidney.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A specific hormone is responsible for causing a disease that is characterized by excessive urination. The urine analysis of such a person reveals that the urine is dilute, has high pH and absence of sugar in it. This is due to under secretion of hormone from
options: The gland which is heterocrine in nature
The gland which stores the hypothalamic hormones
The gland situated on the dorsal side of the forebrain
The gland which is influenced by the hypothalamic hormones
questions.solution:
The hormone responsible for diabetes Insipidus in humans is vasopressin or anti-diuretic hormone (ADH). An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water loss and dehydration.

ADH is released by the posterior pituitary gland. It is responsible for the storage of hormones oxytocin and vasopressin secreted by the posterior pituitary. The disease is called diabetes insipidus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following describes the nature of parathormone?
questions.solution: Parathormone (PTH) maintains the total calcium concentration in blood by acting on bone, increasing absorption of calcium in the small intestine and in the kidney. It is a hypercalcemia hormone, meaning it increases the calcium levels in the blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding ACTH?
options: It is secreted by the anterior lobe of pituitary.
It regulates skin pigmentation in human beings.
It acts on the adrenal cortex and it mainly stimulates the secretion of mineralocorticoids.
Its hypersecretion causes bronze-like pigmentation of skin.
questions.solution: Adrenocorticotropin or adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH): It is secreted by corticotroph cells of the anterior pituitary. It is made up of 39 amino acid polypeptides. Its secretion is prompted by a corticotrophin-release hormone (CRH) of the hypothalamus. Its role is to intensify synthesis of adrenal cortical hormones, particularly the glucocorticoids. The secretion of ACTH is stimulated by low blood level of glucose, shock conditions and presence of a compound called interleukin-1 (IL-1) secreted by macrophages.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Formation of corpus luteum is influenced by
questions.solution: During ovulation, the mature follicle bursts and the ovum is released. After ovulation, the granulosa cells and the interstitial cells form a mass of large and yellowish conical cells. This is named as corpus luteum and serves as a temporary endocrine gland by releasing progesterone and oestrogen. If fertilization takes place, corpus luteum persists and enlarges by influence of LH (Luteinizing hormone).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
How many of the following are examples of hormones which interact with intracellular receptors?

(cortisol, testosterone, estradiol, thyroxine, insulin, epinephrine)
questions.solution: Steroid hormones interact directly with the intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression or chromosome function by interaction of hormone receptor complex with the genome, e.g. cortisol, testosterone, estradiol, progesterone. Also thyroid hormones interact with intra cellular receptors.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A 35 year old man has extremely long limbs and digits. He also has severe disfigurement of the facial features. Which of the following could be a probable cause for it?
options: Hypersecretion of a hormone from neurohypophysis
Hypersecretion of a hormone from adenohypophysis
Hypersecretion of a hormone from thyroid gland
Hypersecretion of a hormone from adrenal gland
questions.solution: The person is suffering from acromegaly. It is a condition seen in middle aged adults as a result of hypersecretion of growth hormone from the anterior pituitary, i.e., adenohypophysis. It is characterized by excessive growth of body, extremely long limbs and digits and severe disfigurement of facial features. It can lead to premature death.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A female is having excessive weight gain in spite of having adequate balanced diet. She also complains of fatigue and tiredness. Her menstrual cycle is also irregular since past few months. Which of the following conditions is she suffering from?
questions.solution: Thyroid hormones T3 and T4 are responsible for maintaining basal metabolic rate. Hypothyroidism leads to decreased BMR which causes excessive weight gain, fatigue, tiredness, palpitations and also irregular menstrual cycle. Tetany is caused due to deficiency of parathormone, and diabetes mellitus is caused due to deficiency of insulin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which cells of the pancreas are responsible for releasing a hormone that increases the rate of glycogenolysis?
questions.solution:
Glucagon:
It is a peptide hormone.
Glucagon acts mainly on the liver cells (hepatocytes).
It increases blood sugar (hyperglycemia) to maintain the normal blood glucose levels by:

A. Stimulating glycogenolysis.
B. Stimulating the process of gluconeogenesis.
C. Reducing cellular glucose uptake and utilisation.

All the above functions clearly indicate that the glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The iodine derivative of amino acid tyrosine brings about effects on target cells by
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Thyroxine is a lipid-soluble hormone, which diffuses into the cell, where it binds to intracellular receptors, migrate to the nucleus, and activate specific target sequences of DNA. Thyroxine is a hormone produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine is important in controlling both development and maturation. It also controls metabolism in adult organisms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements about adrenal hormones. Select the correct one.
options: Aldosterone stimulates the reabsorption of Ca<sup>2+</sup> and water from the renal tubules.
Glucocorticoids promote cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids.
Androgens helps in the maintenance of body fluid volume and osmotic pressure only.
questions.solution: Aldosterone stimulates the reabsorption of <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">N</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and water from renal tubules. Glucocorticoids inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Aldosterone helps in the maintenance of body fluid volume, electrolytes, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Vasopressin is produced and secreted by
questions.solution: Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores, and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates the reabsorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules and thereby reduces the loss of water through urine (diuresis). Hence, it is also called an anti-diuretic hormone (ADH).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
I. Pineal gland is located on the _______A_____side of forebrain.
II. Underproduction of hormones of GH leads to ______B______.
III. Glucagon is a _______C_______ hormone.
options:
A B C
ventral Cushing’s Hypoglycemic

A B C
ventral Pituitary dwarfism Hyperglycemic
questions.solution: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. Glucagon is antagonistic to insulin. The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is not a symptom of exophthalmic goiter?
questions.solution: Exophthalmic goitre (Grave's disease) is thyroid enlargement in which the thyroid secretes excessive amount of thyroid hormones. It is characterized by protrusion of eye balls because of fluid accumulation behind them, loss of weight, rapid heart beat, nervousness, restlessness.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is a hyperglycemic hormone?
questions.solution:
Glucagon is a hormone that is produced by alpha cells in a part of the pancreas known as the islets of Langerhans. When glucagon is released it can perform the following tasks :

A. Stimulating the liver to break down glycogen to be released into the blood as glucose

B. Activating gluconeogenesis, the conversion of amino acids into glucose

C. Breaking down stored fat (triglycerides) into fatty acids for use as fuel by cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these pairs of hormones are not antagonistic in their action?
options: Blood pressure regulation: Aldosterone and Atrial Natriuretic Factor
questions.solution: Parathormone increases the calcium levels in the blood, while calcitonin decreases the calcium levels in the blood; hence, they are antagonistic. Glucagon increases glucose levels in the blood, while insulin decreases glucose levels in the blood; hence, they are antagonistic. Aldosterone increases blood pressure, while ANF decreases blood pressure; hence, they are antagonistic. Both thyroxine and erythropoietin stimulate erythropoiesis, and hence, they are synergistic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Complete the following paragraph by selecting the correct option for the blanks A, B, and C.

The thymus gland is located between the lungs behind the sternum on the .........A........ side of the aorta. .............B.......... secreted by the gland plays a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes which provide ........C............ They also promote antibody production which provides.......D.........
options: A: dorsal, B: Thymic humoral factor, C: humoral immunity, D: cell-mediated immunity
A: ventral, B: Thymopoietin, C: humoral immunity, D: cell-mediated immunity
A: ventral, B: Thymosin, C: cell-mediated immunity, D: humoral immunity
A: dorsal, B: Thymic humoral factor, C: cell-mediated immunity, D: humoral immunity
questions.solution: The thymus gland is located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta. Thymosins secreted by the gland play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes which provide cell-mediated immunity. They also promote antibody production which provides humoral immunity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following hormone helps in maintaining body temperature, metabolism, pigmentation, and defense capabilities?
questions.solution: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body. For example, it helps in maintaining the normal rhythms of sleep-wake cycle, body temperature. In addition, melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle as well as our defense capability.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The alpha and beta cells are found in
questions.solution: Islets of Langerhans is endocrine part of pancreas which contains alpha cells, beta cells and delta cells. Pancreatic acini cells secrete pancreatic enzymes. The ducts carry the secretions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the correct combination of labelling that depicts the hormonal control of the female reproductive system.
options: A - GnRH, B - TSH, C - LTH, D - uterus
A - GnRH, B - STH, C - LH, D - uterus
A - GnRH, B - ACTH, C - LH, D - uterus
A - GnRH, B - LH/FSH, C- estrogen or progesterone, D - uterus
questions.solution: Oogenesis occurs under the influence of hormones. GnRH is secreted by the hypothalamus which stimulates the anterior lobe of pituitary gland to secrete LH and FSH. FSH stimulates the growth of the ovarian follicles and also increases the development of egg/oocyte within the follicle to complete the meiosis I to form secondary oocyte. FSH also stimulates the formation of estrogens. LH stimulates the corpus luteum to secrete progesterone. Ovulation is induced by LH. Both estrogen and progesterone then act on uterus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Hormones which interact with the membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell but generate second messengers. These second messengers are referred as
questions.solution:
Second messengers are intracellular signalling molecules released by the cell in response to exposure to extracellular signalling molecules: the first messengers.

Examples of second messenger molecules include cyclic AMP, cyclic GMP, inositol trisphosphate, diacylglycerol and calcium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the odd one with respect to the chemical nature of a hormone?
questions.solution: Chemically, the hormone may be a peptide, polypeptide (insulin), steroid (cortisol), iodothyronine (thyroid hormones) or amino acid derivative (epinephrine).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements about the parathyroid gland and identify the true and false ones. Select the correct option after referring to the given table.

I. Human beings have a pair of parathyroid glands, situated in each lobe of the thyroid gland.
II. The secretion of PTH is regulated by the levels of circulating calcium ions.
III. PTH is a hypocalcemic hormone.
IV. PTH plays a major role in maintaining calcium balance in the body along with TCT.
options: I- True, II- False, III- True, IV- False
I- True, II-True, III- False, IV- True
I- False, II- False, III- True, IV- False
I- False, II- True, III- False, IV- True
questions.solution:
I. Human beings have four parathyroid glands, two pairs each situated in each lobe of the thyroid gland.

III. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption and also stimulates the absorption of calcium from the renal tubules and digested food. Hence, it is a 'hypercalcemic' hormone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the endocrine glands given in column I with their respective hormones in column II and the functions performed by those hormones in column III and select the correct option from the codes given below.
 
No. Endocrine gland No. Hormone No. Column III (Functions)
I Neuorohypophysis A Cortisol a Hypocalcemic hormone
II Adrenal cortex B PTH b Prevents excessive urination
III Thyroid gland C Vasopressin c Hypercalcemic hormone
IV Parathyroid gland D TCT d Anti-inflammatory reaction and suppression of immune response
questions.solution:
I. Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) secretes the hormone vasopressin, also known as anti-diuretic hormone (ADH). This hormone is responsible for reabsorption of water from the renal tubules and hence prevents excessive urination.

II. Adrenal cortex is responsible for secretion of hormone 'cortisol' which is a major glucocorticoid. It is responsible for anti-inflammatory reaction and suppression of immune response.

III. Thyroid gland secretes the hormone thyrocalcitonin (TCT). It is prevents resorption of calcium from the bones. It is a 'hypocalcemic hormone'.

IV. Parathyroid gland secretes parathyroid hormone (PTH). It is rresponsible for resorption if calcium from the bones and also prevents urinary excretion of calcium. Hence, it is a 'hypercalcemic hormone'.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hormones which increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating are
questions.solution: Adrenaline is derived from catecholamines, which are amino acid derivatives. They are secreted in response to the stress of any kind and during emergency situations.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a ductless gland ?
questions.solution: Exocrine glands or duct glands are glands that secrete substances onto an epithelial surface through a duct. Examples of exocrine glands include sweat, salivary, mammary, ceruminous, lacrimal, sebaceous, prostate and mucous.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following gland is located on the dorsal side of the heart and aorta?
questions.solution: The thymus gland is a small organ behind the breastbone that plays an important function both in the immune system and endocrine system. Though the thymus begins to atrophy (decay) during puberty, its effect in 'training' T-lymphocytes to fight infections, and even cancer, lasts for a lifetime.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following hormones plays a very important role in the regulation of diurnal rhythm of our body?
questions.solution: Melatonin is created by the pineal gland in the brain. In a healthy, normally functioning individual, melatonin is released in a rhythmic cycle, with more melatonin produced at night when the light entering the eyes starts to diminish. The bloodstream carries it to the different areas of the body, where receptors pick up the melatonin to signal the need for sleep.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following secretes luteinizing hormone?
questions.solution: Basophil cells of pars distalis or anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) secrete a luteinizing hormone which is responsible for maintenance of corpus luteum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is related to the pituitary gland?
options: It is located in a depression created by bony cavity.
The anterior pituitary is also called adenohypophysis.
Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone.
questions.solution: The pituitary gland is a pea-sized oval structure, suspended from the underside of the brain by the pituitary stalk (known as the infundibulum). It sits within a small depression in the sphenoid bone, known as the sella turcica (''Turkish saddle''). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis, and pars intermedia. Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH). However, in humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct about the thyroid gland?
options: It is composed of two lobes situated on either side of the oesophagus.
The follicular cells of the thyroid gland are responsible for secretion of hormones.
Exopthalmic goitre is a form of hypothyroidism.
Hyperthyroidism during pregnancy can cause defective foetal development.
questions.solution:
1. The thyroid gland is a gland made up of two lobes. Each lobe is situated on the either side of the trachea.

2. The follicular cells of the thyroid gland are responsible for secretion of the thyroid hormones T3 and T4. These cells are present in the stroma. They have a substance known as colloid.

3. Exopthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism.

4. Hypothyroidism during pregnancy can cause defective foetal development.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: According to the accepted concept of hormone action, if receptor molecules are removed from target organs, then the target organ will
options: Continue to respond to the hormone without any difference
Continue to respond to the hormone but in the opposite way
Continue to respond to the hormone but will require higher concentration
questions.solution: The hormones in blood act on specific sites or receptors of target organ, so if we remove the receptor molecule from the target organs, there will be no response.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The diagram given below is related to which of the following set of hormones?
questions.solution: All lipid-soluble hormones such as adrenocorticoids, steroidal, and Iodothyronines hormones can easily cross the target cell membrane and enter inside the target cell. These hormones bind to their specific intracellular receptor to form the hormone–receptor complex, which ultimately binds to DNA and regulates gene expressions to give the physiological response.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Consider the following match of hormones and select the incorrect one:
options: Cortisol: Anti-inflammatory, immuno-suppressive and stimulate RBC production.
Thyroxine: Regulate <math><mtext>BMR</mtext></math>, maintain water-electrolyte balance and support RBC formation.
Adrenaline: Prepare body for emergency or  <math><mtext>'3 F'</mtext></math>  conditions.
Calcitonin: Decreases bone calcium level in human body.
questions.solution: Glucocorticoids, mainly cortisol hormone, produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppress the immune response. They also stimulate <math><mtext>RBC</mtext></math> production. Adrenaline or epinephrine is secreted from the adrenal medulla in response to stress or emergency or fight, flight and fright conditions. Thyroxine regulates BMR, maintains water-electrolyte balance and supports RBC formation. Thyrocalcitonin (TCT) is a long peptide hormone secreted by parafollicular cells of the thyroid gland (C-cells). Its secretion is regulated by an increased plasma level of calcium by a feedback mechanism. TCT lowers calcium level in the blood to normal by increasing calcium deposition in the bones, so it checks osteoporosis and stimulates excretion of calcium in the urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?

1. The hormone responsible for maintaining the diurnal rhythm of the body is secreted by a gland situated on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
2. Exophthalmic goitre is characterized by protrusion of eyeballs, weight loss, enlargement of the thyroid gland and decreased basal metabolic rate.
3. Addison's disease occurs due to decreased production of hormones from the outer part of the adrenal gland.
4. Hypersecretion of parathormone causes an increase in the deposition of calcium in bones.
questions.solution:
The hormone responsible for maintaining the diurnal rhythm of the body is melatonin. It is secreted by the pineal gland, which is situated on the dorsal side of the forebrain.

Exopthalmic goitre is characterized by protrusion of eyeballs, weight loss, enlargement of thyroid gland and an increased basal metabolic rate. This increased basal metabolic rate is the cause for excessive weight loss.

Addison's disease is a condition occurring due to decreased secretion of hormones from the adrenal cortex i.e. the outer part of adrenal gland. It is characterized by a lot of weakness and fatigue.

Hypersecretion of parathormone causes decrease in the deposition of calcium in bones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hormone which regulates the growth of mammary glands and formation of milk in them is secreted by
options: The gland attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk
The gland situated at the base of diencephalon
The gland situated near the trachea
The gland situated near the aorta
questions.solution: The hormone which regulates the growth of mammary glands and formation of milk in them is prolactin. Prolactin is secreted by the pituitary gland, which is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk. The gland situated at the base of diencephalon is hypothalamus. The gland situated near the aorta is thymus which secretes thymosine which helps in maturation of T- lymphocytes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the pituitary gland of an adult rat is surgically removed, which of the following endocrine glands will be the least affected?
questions.solution:
The anterior lobe of pituitary gland secretes Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), which controls the structure, and functioning of thyroid and Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH) which controls the structure and functioning of the adrenal cortex. Besides, it secretes FSH, LH, ICSH, etc, which affect the structure and functioning of gonads.

So, if the pituitary gland of an adult rat is surgically removed, out of the four options adrenal medulla will be less affected.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Thymosin is the peptide hormone secreted by the thymus gland. This hormone stimulates the development of T-cells or T lymphocytes. Thymus is the place where the T-cells gets activated as they are produced in bone marrow cells.

questions.solution: Exophthalmic goitre (Craves' disease) is thyroid enlargement in which the thyroid secretes excessive amount of thyroid hormones. questions.solution: Adrenal cortex secretes many hormones collectively known as Corticoids. This hormone acts on kidneys and enhances reabsorption of sodium and water in order to decrease their excretion. questions.q: Polydipsia, hyperglycemia and polyuria occur due to
questions.solution: Pancreas is composite or heterocrine glands as they contain both endocrine and exocrine glandular tissues. Endocrine tissue is made up of small clusters of cells known as Islets of Langerhans which has two types of cells: Alpha cells that secrete glucagon and Beta cells that secrete insulin. Both these hormones together carry out Glucose metabolism. Glucagon carries out glycogenolysis and Insulin is responsible for cellular uptake of glucose. If insulin levels are not adequate the cellular uptake of glucose is affected or in other words transport of glucose from blood into cells is affected due to which blood glucose level rises. This is known as Diabetes mellitus. Polyuria (increase urination), Polydipsia (increased thirst) and polyphagia (increased hunger are symptoms of diabetes mellitus)

questions.solution: Foetal ejection reflex is an accelerated active labour and birth which is induced by release of oxytocin from pituitary. Oxytocin (child birth hormone), secreted by neurohypophysis of pituitary gland, stimulates contraction of uterus muscles, including labour pain for child birth, when secretion of progesterone hormone declines, making the end of pregnancy. questions.q: Which of the following hormones are secreted by pars nervosa?
questions.solution:
Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to neurohypophysis. 
 
• Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction. In females, it stimulates a vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of childbirth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland. 
 
• Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates the resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules and thereby reduces the loss of water through urine (diuresis). Hence, it is also called an anti-diuretic hormone (ADH).

questions.q: Diabetes is one of the most common lifestyle disorders in India, which is successfully treated with insulin therapy which reduces the blood glucose level. Which of the following mechanisms correctly shows the action of insulin in lowering blood glucose level?
options: It stimulates the breakdown of glycogen.
It stimulates the process of gluconeogenesis.
It acts on adipocytes and hepatocytes and increase cellular glucose uptake and utilization.

questions.solution: Insulin and Glucagon are two main hormones that bring about glucose metabolism in humans. Glucagon is secreted by alpha cells of islets of langerhans that are small clusters of endocrine cells in pancreas and Insulin is released by beta cells of pancreas. Glucagon brings about breakdown of glycogen into glucose and thus increases the level of glucose in blood. Insulin further carries this glucose to different cells and thus reduces blood glucose level. After cellular uptake too if the glucose levels are high in the blood insulin causes mobilization of glucose from blood into hepatocytes and adipocytes where it gets converted into glycogen which is the reserve form.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The primary target of the hormones of hypothalamus is
questions.solution: The hypothalamus is the floor of diencephalon which is a part of forebrain. It contains many neurosecretory cells which secrete hormones. These hormones control formation and secretion of pituitary hormones. Pituitary gland is attached to hypothalamus via stalk known as infundibulum. Pituitary gland is made up of two lobes: Adenohypophysis and Neurohypophysis and both these parts are dependent on the hypothalamus. Hypothalamus secrets various releasing and inhibiting hormones which bring about release of hormones of anterior pituitary which is a part of adenohypophysis. Neurohypophysis does not produce any hormone of its own but stores hormones of the hypothalamus. Thus primary target of hypothalamus is pituitary gland also known as hypophysis or master endocrine gland. Hence hypothalamus is regarded as master of master endocrine gland.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hormone that stimulates the stomach to secrete gastric juice is
questions.solution:
Endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastrointestinal tract secrete four major peptide hormones, namely gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin (CCK) and gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP). Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and
motility.

questions.solution:
Hypothyroidism: It commonly results from the deficiency of iodine in our diet and is characterized by the enlargement of the thyroid gland (or goitre).

Hypothyroidism during pregnancy: Cretinism. [In cretinism, after birth the growing baby suffers from stunted growth (cretinism), mental retardation, low intelligence quotient, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism, etc.]

Hypothyroidism in adult women: Irregular menstrual cycle.

Melatonin: 1. Melatonin is very important for the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body.

Example: It helps in maintaining the normal rhythms of sleep-wake cycle, body temperature, etc.

2. It also affects - metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle and our immune system.

The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH).

Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules and thereby reduces loss of water through urine (diuresis). Hence, it is also called as anti-diuretic hormone (ADH).

questions.solution:

Hormones like FSH do not enter the target cell. They interact with the membrane-bound receptors and generate secondary messengers like cyclic AMP for their action.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The alpha and beta cells are found in:
questions.solution: The endocrine pancreas consists of ‘Islets of Langerhans’. There are about 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans in a normal human pancreas representing only 1 to 2 percent of the pancreatic tissue. The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called alpha-cells, beta-cells, delta cells and PP cells. The alpha-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the beta-cells secrete insulin. Delta cells producing somatostatin (3–10%), while PP cells (gamma cells) producing pancreatic polypeptide

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not the function of insulin?
options: Increases the oxidation of glucose in the cells
Initiates the conversion of glycogen to glucose
Increases the permeability of cell membrane to glucose
Initiates the formation of animal storage polysaccharide.
questions.solution:

1. It is responsible for increasing the oxidation of glucose in the cells.

2. It increases the permeability of the cell membrane to glucose.

3. It causes the conversion of excess glucose to glycogen, which is stored in the liver.

The hormone which initiates the conversion of glycogen to glucose is glycogen.

About 20 steroids (steroidogenic) compounds are secreted from the adrenal cortex and these are called adrenocorticoids or corticosteroids. questions.q: Identify the hormone with its correct matching of source and function.

questions.solution:
Circadian rhythm is a 24-hour sleep-wake cycle. It is controlled by hormone melatonin. Melatonin is secreted by pineal gland. This gland is attached via a stalk with the epithalamus and hence it is also known as epiphysis. It is also known as the third eye as this gland is present at the axis traced from the third eye. Melatonin secretion depends on light. It increases due to darkness and decreases due to light.

ANF is secreted by atria and it decreases the blood pressure raised due to RAAS. Oxytocin is the birth hormone as it plays an important role during parturition and milk production. Growth and maintenance of mammary glands is by sex hormones after puberty and by prolactin during pregnancy. Progesterone and Estrogen are secreted by the corpus luteum and these are responsible for repair of the endometrium of the uterus.

questions.solution:
The hormone which is responsible for conversion of excessive glucose present in the body into glycogen is insulin. Glycogen is stored in the liver. Insulin is produced by the beta cells of Islet of Langerhans of pancreas.

Thymus is responsible for production of thymosins, which help in maturation of T lymphocytes.

questions.solution:
Calcitonin, also known as Thyrocalcitonin is a hormone produced by the thyroid gland. The function of this hormone is to prevent the reabsorption of calcium from the bones. Thus, it is responsible for decreasing blood calcium levels.

Thyroxine, also known as Tetraiodothyronine (T4) is a hormone secreted by the thyroid gland. This hormone is responsible for increasing the basal metabolic rate of the body and regulating it.

Glucagon is a hormone secreted by alpha cells of Islet of Langerhans of pancreas. It increases blood sugar levels by stimulating glycogenolysis.

Glucocorticoids are hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex. They stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which region of the adrenal gland is responsible for the secretion of catecholamines?
questions.solution: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration. Catecholamines also stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in blood. In addition, they also stimulate the breakdown of lipids and proteins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following sentences and then answer the question given below.

I. Parathyroid hormone regulates the metabolism of calcium.
II. Vasopressin is also called anti-diuretic hormone.
III. Grave's disease is caused by malfunctioning of the adrenal gland.
IV. Oxytocin facilitates parturition by acting on the middle layer of the uterus which is made-up of striated involuntary muscles.

Which of the above statements are correct and incorrect?
questions.solution:
Exophthalmic goiter is a form of hyperthyroidism, characterized by enlargement of the thyroid gland, protrusion of the eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate, and weight loss also called Graves’ disease. It is an autoimmune disorder.

Anti-diuretic hormone or vasopressin increases the reabsorption of water in the distal convoluted tubule and collecting ducts of the nephrons of the kidneys. Hence, it reduces the amount of urine formation.

Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles (non-striated involuntary muscles) of our body and stimulates their contraction. In females, it encourages a vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of childbirth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland.

Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/ demineralisation). PTH also stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and increases Ca2+ absorption from the digested food. It is, thus, clear that PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone, i.e., it increases the blood Ca2+ levels. Along with TCT, it plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Given below is a schematic representation of the mechanism of hormone action. Select the set of hormones which can bind with Y.
questions.solution: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors (for peptide hormones) and the receptors present inside the target cell (for steroid and amino derived hormones) are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). Binding of a hormone to its receptor leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex. Testosterone, estrogen are steroidal hormones which can cross through the plasma membrane, reach DNA in the nucleus and directly stimulate transcription.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the sugar level of blood is too high, it can be reduced immediately by
questions.solution: Insulin and Glucagon are pancreatic hormones that control sugar metabolism. Insulin is responsible for lowering the blood sugar level as it increases cellular uptake of glucose. Thus it transports glucose from the blood into the cells. In IDDM (Insulin dependent diabetes mellitus) the insulin production is impaired due to which glucose accumulates in the blood. This will increase the viscosity of blood and will hamper the blood flow. This condition can be corrected  by intravenous insulin and thus insulin will directly enter the blood and thus reduce the blood sugar. Insulin cannot be given orally because insulin is proteinaceous hormone and proteins easily dissolve in the stomach.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body. For example, it helps in maintaining the normal rhythms of the sleep-wake cycle, body temperature. In addition, melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle, as well as our defense capability.

Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produce anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production.

glucagon from alpha cells of pancreas
questions.solution: When the blood glucose level goes down, glucagon is secreted by the alpha cells of pancreas. Glucagon signals the liver to break down glycogen to glucose and release it into the blood stream. Thus bringing the level of glucose back to normal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
As part of a student project, Sheela surgically made a full cut in the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract (infundibulum) in pregnant rabbits and studied the physiological effect on different tissues/organs. Which of the following should be expected?

(i) Formation of a large volume of dilute urine
(ii) Increased blood sugar levels
(iii) Increased heart rate
(iv) Difficulty in parturition
questions.solution: Pituitary gland is the master endocrine gland of the body. It is connected to hypothalamus which is a part of the forebrain. Hypothalamus controls the pituitary gland and thus it is known as Master of master endocrine gland. Pituitary gland consists of two lobes: Adenohypophysis and Neurohypophysis. Neurohypophysis is also known as posterior pituitary and it is connected to the hypothalamus through infundibulum or pituitary stalk. Hypothalamic nuclei secretes two hormones which are stored in the posterior pituitary in hassall's corpuscles. These two hormones are ADH and Oxytocin. Hence if the stalk is cut these two hormones will not be stored in the posterior part and thus will not be able to perform its function. If ADH secretion decreases, water reabsorption will be affected and thus dilute urine will be formed. Oxytocin is the birth hormone as it plays an important role during parturition and milk production. In the question the rabbit is pregnant and hence if the infundibulum is cut there will be no oxytocin release and this will affect parturition.
